name: Smash Burgers
blurb: Thin, crispy-edged beef patties with melted cheese in a soft bun.
ingredients: 600g beef mince (20% fat), loosely formed into 8 balls
Burger sauce: 4 tbsp mayo, 2 tbsp ketchup, 1 tbsp mustard, 1 tbsp chopped gherkin
method: Get a heavy pan or flat griddle smoking hot.
Put a ball of mince in the pan, scatter with a little onion, and smash flat with a spatula for 15 seconds. Season.
Cook 2 minutes until the edges are lacy and crisp, flip, add cheese and cook 1 minute more.
Stack two patties per toasted bun with sauce, pickles and lettuce.

name: Baked Mac & Cheese
blurb: Ultra-cheesy macaroni with a crunchy buttered crumb, US diner style.
ingredients: 200g sharp cheddar, 100g Monterey Jack or mozzarella, 40g parmesan
1 tsp mustard powder, 1/2 tsp smoked paprika
method: Cook the macaroni 2 minutes under, then drain.
Make a roux with the butter and flour, whisk in the milk and simmer to a smooth sauce.
Off the heat stir in the cheeses, mustard powder and paprika.
Combine with the pasta, tip into a dish, top with the panko and bake at 200C fan for 20 minutes.

name: Buffalo Wings
blurb: Baked-then-tossed wings in a buttery hot sauce with blue cheese dip.
ingredients: 80g butter, 120ml hot sauce (Frank's style), 1 tsp Worcestershire
Blue cheese dip: 80g blue cheese, 3 tbsp soured cream, 3 tbsp mayo, splash of milk
Celery and carrot sticks to serve
method: Pat the wings very dry, toss with the baking powder and salt, and arrange on a rack.
Bake at 220C fan for 40-45 minutes, turning once, until deeply crisp.
Melt the butter with the hot sauce and Worcestershire.
Toss the hot wings in the sauce and serve with the blue cheese dip and crudites.

name: BBQ Pulled Pork
blurb: Low and slow pork shoulder with a dry rub, pulled and sauced, in buns.
ingredients: Rub: 3 tbsp brown sugar, 2 tbsp smoked paprika, 1 tbsp each salt, pepper, garlic powder, mustard powder
BBQ sauce: 200ml ketchup, 3 tbsp cider vinegar, 2 tbsp brown sugar, 1 tbsp Worcestershire, 1 tsp smoked paprika
Soft buns and slaw to serve
method: Rub the pork all over and leave overnight if you can.
Sit it in a deep tray, pour the cider around, cover tightly with foil and cook at 140C fan for 5 hours until it shreds with a fork.
Rest 30 minutes, then pull the meat, discarding excess fat.
Simmer the sauce ingredients for 10 minutes and toss enough through the pork to coat.
Pile into buns with slaw.

name: Classic Meatloaf
blurb: Herby beef and pork loaf with a sticky ketchup glaze, with mash.
ingredients: 2 tbsp Worcestershire, 1 tbsp Dijon, 1 tsp thyme
Glaze: 100ml ketchup, 2 tbsp brown sugar, 1 tbsp cider vinegar
Mash and green beans to serve
method: Soak the breadcrumbs in the milk. Mix with the minces, onion, garlic, eggs, Worcestershire, mustard and thyme. Season.
Press into a loaf tin or shape on a lined tray.
Bake at 180C fan for 40 minutes, then brush with the glaze and bake 20 minutes more.
Rest 10 minutes, slice, and serve with mash and beans.

name: Chicken & Sausage Jambalaya
blurb: One-pot Louisiana rice with chicken, smoked sausage and the holy trinity.
ingredients: 1 onion, 1 green pepper, 2 celery sticks, diced
2 tbsp Cajun seasoning, 1 tsp smoked paprika
method: Brown the chicken and sausage, then set aside.
Soften the onion, pepper and celery, then add the Cajun seasoning and paprika.
Stir in the rice, then the tomatoes and stock, and return the meat.
Cover and simmer for 20-25 minutes until the rice is tender and the liquid absorbed.
Rest 5 minutes and finish with spring onions.

name: Philly Cheesesteak
blurb: Thin-sliced steak with onions and molten cheese in a soft sub roll.
ingredients: 600g rump or ribeye, part-frozen and shaved thin
method: Fry the onions (and pepper) in a hot pan until soft and browned, then push to one side.
Add the shaved beef, season, and cook quickly, chopping it up with the edge of a spatula.
Mix the beef and onions, divide into roll-sized piles, lay cheese over each and let it melt.
Scoop each pile into a buttered, toasted roll.

name: Chili with Cornbread
blurb: A thick beef and bean chili baked under a cornbread topping.
ingredients: 2 tbsp smoked paprika, 1 tbsp cumin, 1 tsp chipotle paste
400g tin chopped tomatoes, 400g tin kidney beans
Cornbread: 150g cornmeal, 100g flour, 1 tbsp baking powder, 1 egg, 250ml buttermilk, 40g melted butter, 1 tsp sugar
method: Brown the mince, add the onion, pepper, garlic and spices, then the tomatoes and beans. Simmer 30 minutes until thick.
Tip into a wide ovenproof dish.
Whisk the cornbread wet and dry ingredients separately, then combine to a thick batter.
Dollop over the chili and bake at 190C fan for 25 minutes until the topping is set and golden.

name: Sloppy Joes
blurb: Sweet-savoury saucy beef mince piled into soft burger buns.
ingredients: 1 onion and 1 green pepper, finely diced
4 tbsp ketchup, 1 tbsp tomato puree, 1 tbsp brown sugar, 1 tbsp Worcestershire, 1 tsp mustard
method: Brown the mince, add the onion, pepper and garlic and cook until soft.
Stir in the ketchup, puree, sugar, Worcestershire and mustard, then the stock.
Simmer for 10-12 minutes until thick and glossy.
Spoon generously into toasted buns.

name: New England Clam Chowder
blurb: Creamy potato and clam soup with bacon, served with crackers.
ingredients: 2 x 400g tins clams in juice (or 1kg fresh, steamed)
Oyster or saltine crackers to serve
method: Fry the bacon until crisp, then soften the onion and celery in the fat.
Stir in the flour, then add the clam juice, potatoes, bay and thyme, and simmer until the potatoes are tender.
Add the milk and cream and warm through without boiling.
Stir in the clams, season, and serve with crackers and parsley.

name: Chicken Pot Pie
blurb: Creamy chicken and vegetables under a flaky pastry lid.
method: Brown the chicken, then soften the onion, carrot and celery.
Stir in the flour, then the stock, and simmer to a sauce. Add the cream, thyme, peas, sweetcorn and chicken.
Tip into a pie dish and cool a little.
Top with pastry, crimp, glaze with egg, cut a vent, and bake at 200C fan for 25-30 minutes.

name: Chicken Cobb Salad
blurb: A big composed salad of chicken, bacon, egg, avocado and blue cheese.
ingredients: Dressing: 4 tbsp olive oil, 2 tbsp red wine vinegar, 1 tsp Dijon, 1 tsp honey
method: Arrange the lettuce on a big platter.
Lay the chicken, bacon, quartered eggs, sliced avocado, tomatoes and crumbled blue cheese in rows on top.
Whisk the dressing and pour over just before serving.
Toss at the table.

name: Tuna Melt
blurb: Griddled sandwich of tuna mayo and melting cheese.
ingredients: 3 tbsp mayo, 1 tbsp chopped gherkin, 2 spring onions, squeeze of lemon
method: Mix the tuna with the mayo, gherkin, spring onion and lemon; season.
Butter the bread on the outside. Build sandwiches with cheese, tuna, cheese.
Griddle in a pan over medium heat for 3-4 minutes each side, pressing, until golden and molten.

name: Loaded Hot Dogs
blurb: Griddled frankfurters in soft buns with quick onions and all the sauces.
ingredients: 2 onions, sliced and fried until sticky
method: Griddle or fry the sausages until browned and hot through.
Lightly toast the buns.
Load with the fried onions and sausages.
Finish with mustard, ketchup and whatever toppings you like.
